extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in fluid mechanics and applied machine learning
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for applying machine learning methods to problems in fluid mechanics, including algorithm selection, data considerations, modeling trade-offs, and verification. Focuses on what makes ML solutions suitable, reliable, and scientifically useful in fluid-dynamics contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which a model may be understood or interpreted by an expert human.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper states interpretability is essential in fluid dynamics where deeper understanding of mechanisms is often required. Prefer models or methods (or post-hoc analysis) that provide human-understandable insight rather than only black-box predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of a model to generalize to new examples including unseen data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review emphasizes that models must generalize beyond training data; explicitly consider whether the model is to be used for interpolation within a parameter regime or for extrapolation, which is considerably more challenging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance guarantees and theoretical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of guarantees on performance, convergence results, and theoretical understanding of the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors stress that guarantees are often rare and that work should aim to provide convergence results, analysis, and bounds where possible to increase trust in ML methods applied to fluids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-validation and overfitting prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of withheld datasets and cross-validation to prevent overfitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review explicitly highlights the importance of cross-validation on withheld data sets to prevent overfitting in machine learning applications to fluid mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of domain knowledge / hybrid methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate knowledge about fluid mechanics into learning algorithms or combine ML with first-principles models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article ‘highlights the benefit of incorporating domain knowledge’ and envisions hybrid methods combining machine learning and first principles models as fertile ground; use physics constraints, invariances, or model structure to improve performance and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of loss function balancing learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of loss L that balances objectives such as accuracy, simplicity, smoothness, sparsity, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the risk functional R(w): 'the loss function L balances the various learning objectives (e.g., accuracy, simplicity, smoothness, etc.)'. Choose loss/regularizers to reflect desired trade-offs (e.g., sparsity, smoothness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of data distribution p(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that the risk functional is weighted by the input–output distribution p(x,y), which constrains predictive capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes 'the risk functional is weighted by a probability distribution p(x,y) that also constrains the predictive capabilities of the learning machine' — thus ensure training data match target deployment distribution, or account for distribution shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample efficiency and data-cost awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for limited or expensive data: experiments may be hard to repeat, simulations may be costly, and data can be sparse in some dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review warns that fluids problems often have expensive evaluations and data that are 'vast in some dimensions ... sparse in others' — choose sample-efficient methods, multi-fidelity approaches, or methods that leverage prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to handle multi-scale and nonlinear phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms must address nonlinearities and multiple spatiotemporal scales present in fluid flows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors point out that fluid flows present complex multi-scale nonlinear behavior that may not be captured by off-the-shelf ML algorithms; prefer architectures and preprocessing that account for scales and nonlinear dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-stationarity handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to deal with non-stationary systems and difficulties in obtaining statistically converged results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many fluid systems are non-stationary, algorithms should be robust to non-stationarity or include mechanisms to adapt/update as statistics change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate architecture selection for data modality
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose model architectures that suit the data type, e.g., RNNs/LSTMs for sequences, CNNs for image-like fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text discusses RNNs and LSTM for time-series and MD-LSTM for spatiotemporal data, and notes issues (vanishing/exploding gradients) and remedies (LSTM, echo state networks). Match architecture to temporal/spatial structure and address training instabilities with regularization and architectural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensionality reduction matched to flow features
rubrics_metrics.description: Select dimensionality-reduction methods (POD/PCA, autoencoders, principal curves, SOMs) appropriate to the flow's features and goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POD/PCA offers linear, invertible relations via eigenproblems; autoencoders allow nonlinear reductions but may lose inverse relationship. The review advises matching the method to the features sought and to downstream tasks (e.g., control, modeling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-off: interpretability vs expressivity in reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance interpretability (e.g., POD/PCA eigenmodes) against expressivity (nonlinear autoencoders and deep representations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors note PCA/POD are interpretable and have analytic solutions, while deep autoencoders can extract nonlinear structure but at potential cost of interpretability and invertibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering vs vector quantization choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide between clustering (discovering groupings) and vector quantization (predetermined representative centers) based on goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper explains vector quantization uses a predetermined number of centers and is for data reduction; clustering seeks meaningful groupings — choose according to whether prototypes or exploratory grouping is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about GAN training stability and convergence; large data helps but equilibrium is not guaranteed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review states 'one must be cautious on whether an equilibrium will ever be reached... there is no guarantee of convergence' and that GANs need large datasets; evaluate GAN suitability carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinforcement learning sample complexity and LTCA
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for RL's high computational cost, long-term credit assignment (LTCA), and sparse/delayed rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper highlights RL 'requires significant computational resources' and LTCA problems; recommends augmenting sparse rewards with dense subgoals, carefully designing value/policy representations, and being mindful of episode requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimization method suitability for expensive evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose optimization/search strategies (ES, GA, CMA-ES, IGO, EDAs) mindful of scaling, convergence guarantees, and the cost of objective evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note iterative distribution-estimation algorithms (CMA-ES, IGO) can be effective but scaling and convergence in complex fluid landscapes remain unclear; prefer methods that handle expensive evaluations (e.g., surrogate or multi-fidelity schemes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed invariances and physical constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Design ML models to respect known invariances, symmetries, and physical constraints of the fluid problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review and cited works argue embedding invariance properties (e.g., rotational/translational invariance, conservation laws) improves prediction and generalization; consider invariant architectures or feature engineering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularization and sparsity for robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use regularization (including sparsity-promoting penalties) to improve robustness and interpretability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative loss functions may reflect constraints such as sparsity; regularize recurrent nets to avoid gradient issues; sparsity can aid interpretability and sensor/feature selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational cost and scalability planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider computational resource requirements (training episodes, HPC needs) and algorithm scalability before selecting methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper repeatedly emphasizes heavy computational demands (deep learning, RL, large-scale simulations), and that scaling of some methods (e.g., EDAs) remains unclear; plan algorithms within resource budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use benchmarks and open-source tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage open source software and benchmark problems to develop, compare, and validate methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The introduction notes an 'abundance of open source software and benchmark problems' and encourages their use for reproducibility, comparison, and community progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for physical insight, not only predictive accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer methods that help quantify underlying physical mechanisms, not only provide accurate predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review stresses the need to 'precisely quantify the underlying physical mechanisms' in fluid flows; models should enable analysis and understanding in addition to prediction.
